lesson.title: Over Their Head
lesson.hook: Two connected choices. Watch what your first shot creates.
lesson.liveIntro: They have closed much nearer the net and cover the passing angles. You have room to lift the ball.

tb1A.name: What does the next ball give you?
tb1A.sit: Their volley is deeper to your backhand. They still cover the net.
tb1A.q: What does the next ball give you?
opts: Use controlled depth into the open court

lines.A: The space looks inviting, but the deep contact makes forcing it demanding.
lines.B: You give yourself another recovery window from the deeper volley.

tb1A.take: Their net position changes the space. Recover while the lob travels.
tb1A.payoff: Their net position changes the space. Recover while the lob travels.
tb1A.principle: Read how close they stand. Use the space above them.
tb1A.why: A player close to the net can cover many passing angles but leaves space behind. A deep lob is available when your contact supports lift. It is not an automatic winner: this opponent chases it down, and the next ball decides your next action.

tb1B.name: What does the next ball give you?
tb1B.sit: They chase behind the baseline and send a shorter reply. You have recovered with time.
tb1B.q: What does the next ball give you?
opts: Use controlled depth into the open court

lines.A: You use the shorter reply with a generous target. The point continues.
lines.B: A sound reset. The shorter reply also gave you time to apply pressure.

tb1B.take: Their net position changes the space. Recover while the lob travels.
tb1B.payoff: Their net position changes the space. Recover while the lob travels.
tb1B.principle: Read how close they stand. Use the space above them.
tb1B.why: A player close to the net can cover many passing angles but leaves space behind. A deep lob is available when your contact supports lift. It is not an automatic winner: this opponent chases it down, and the next ball decides your next action.

tb1.name: Where is the larger space now?
tb1.sit: They have closed much nearer the net and cover the passing angles. You have room to lift the ball.
tb1.q: Where is the larger space now?
opts: Drive through the angle they are covering
Lift a deep lob over their reach

lines.A: They intercept above the net. Read their volley and find room for the next shot.
lines.B: The lob clears their reach and sends them back. Recover while they chase it.

tb1.take: Their net position changes the space. Recover while the lob travels.
tb1.payoff: Their net position changes the space. Recover while the lob travels.
tb1.principle: Read how close they stand. Use the space above them.
tb1.why: A player close to the net can cover many passing angles but leaves space behind. A deep lob is available when your contact supports lift. It is not an automatic winner: this opponent chases it down, and the next ball decides your next action.

summaries.10: The first choice fitted. The next ball needed a fresh decision.
summaries.11: Both choices fitted the contact and court you had. Keep reading as the point changes.
summaries.01: You adapted on the second ball. Compare what the first choice cost.
summaries.00: Compare the first choice, then read the next contact again. A landing alone does not prove a sound decision.

comparison.summary: Compare what your first choice creates.
comparison.intro: Hold the incoming situation fixed. Change the first shot and watch the reply.

lesson.completionIntro: Your first choice changed the next ball. Read each contact afresh.

pro.label: Read the contact and court
pro.moment: Tennis Australia’s tactical situations connect shot selection to opponent position and available space. This example contrasts a net player’s close position with the previous lower-volley situation.

drill.name: Two-ball read
drill.how: Have a partner vary how close they stand to the net. Choose feet or lob from the position, then continue with whichever reply they reach.
